mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the prior three months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.5% q/q over last 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises by >0.5% q/q.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the unemployment rate below 4.5% for two consecutive months signals labor market overheating, which historically precedes slower earnings growth and higher inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE is below 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline q/q for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average by more than 2% for three consecutive months signals a supply-side expansion, which historically coincides with higher earnings and positive equity returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when INDPRO is above its 12-month MA by >2% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual shock of inflation and policy tightening, which historically reduces risk asset valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 100,000 alongside a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a tight labor market, which historically precedes wage inflation and reduced profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS increases by >100,000 and UNRATE declines in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below its 12-month average for four consecutive months signals reduced household buffer capacity, which historically coincides with lower consumer spending and negative equity returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS is below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly increase of at least 0.5% in both INDPRO and HOUST signals a broad-based expansion in industrial output and housing construction, which typically boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both INDPRO and HOUST rise by >0.5% month-over-month.
